subject: Post-upgrade throughput & latency spike — urgent attention requested
messages:
From: Sam Wells <sam.wells@blueforge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Chu <emily.chu@blueforge.com>, procurement@blueforge.com
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 15:23:00 -0400
Subject: Production degradation after model/quant switch — urgent

Marissa,

We pushed the Redwood-provided model upgrade (v3.2 -> v4beta) with the recommended quant profile earlier this morning. Within ~30 minutes we started seeing a P99 latency jump from ~220ms to 1.8s and a noticeable increase in 5xx errors for our streaming inference path. Throughput dropped by roughly 30% on peak routes and several customer flows are timing out.

Attached are: a filtered log bundle (error-logs-20280517.zip) and a snapshot of our APM showing the p99 spike (dashboard-p99-spike.png). Key observations: 
- Latency jump correlated with requests that hit >512 token decoding windows
- Error rate concentrated on the reranker endpoint (rnk-v2)
- No infra scaling events on our side — CPU/GPU utilization looks nominal

This is affecting production traffic for several important customers. We need to understand whether this is a model-quality issue, quantization-induced performance regression, or a runtime kernel selection problem. Can Redwood create an incident and propose a rollback plan? We are ready to join an urgent call.

—Sam
Sam Wells
CTO, BlueForge
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Wells <sam.wells@blueforge.com>
Cc: Emily Chu <emily.chu@blueforge.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 15:41:12 -0400
Subject: Re: Production degradation after model/quant switch — urgent

Sam — thanks for the detailed callout and the logs. We’ve opened INC-20280517-BF (link below) and are pulling together the on-call infra + runtime team now.

Immediate asks so we can triage quickly:
- Can you paste a couple of request IDs for failures (x-request-id) — the logs you attached look trimmed and we want the original traces
- If you can toggle traffic for the reranker to a sandbox key for a minute, we’ll run a controlled A/B with v3.2 quant profile to validate rollback latency

Rishi / Lauren / Vivek — flagging for commercial + exec attention. If this is a quant-induced regresssion we should be prepared to:
1) rollback the service to the last known-good model/quant pair (v3.2 / qprofile-0.7) on BlueForge’s Dedicated pool,
2) keep v4beta/quant in canary for non-critical routes, and
3) discuss a short-term SLA credit if customer impact is confirmed.

I’m available for a 30-min bridge at 17:00 ET. Sam — does that work for you?

Links: https://redwood-internal.incidents/INC-20280517-BF

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 16:05:34 -0400
Subject: RE: Production degradation after model/quant switch — urgent

Short note from the field: BlueForge is a mid-enterprise customer with a multi-year committed Dedicated contract (deal BF-2024-0912). They are on a usage tier where SLA credits and executive attention matter to renewal.

Proposed next steps (commercial + ops):
- Approve an immediate rollback to v3.2/qprofile-0.7 on their production pool (if the runtime team gives the green light) — low-risk from a billing perspective.
- Offer a 15% service credit for the incident window if rollback does not fully remove customer impact.
- Schedule an executive sync with Sam (CTO) and Emily (VP Product) after triage — propose 17:30 ET so we can include infra lead.

I’ll coordinate the credit paperwork and notify finance if we go ahead. Marissa — if you get a green light from runtime, I’ll prepare the message to BlueForge procurement.

—Rishi
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 18:22:10 -0400
Subject: Exec approval request — rollback + temporary credit authorization

Team — quick directive: prioritize customer availability. If runtime confirms the quant profile is the root cause, authorize rollback without waiting for formal change window. I want an explicit runbook step that freezes traffic to the v4beta variant and flips the routing to v3.2 for affected pools.

Regarding credits: authorize up to 20% credit for the impacted window if rollback is the mitigation. We can refine the amount after a post-incident analysis, but approving up to 20% now will allow Rishi to tell BlueForge we’re committed.

I’ll join the 17:30 ET call and escalate to legal only if BlueForge asks for contract amendments.

—Lauren
VP, Customer Success Ops
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Wells <sam.wells@blueforge.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 May 2028 00:45:02 +0000
Subject: Re: Production degradation after model/quant switch — urgent

Sam — thanks for raising this. We’ve stood up an incident bridge and the runtime team is reproducing the P99 behavior in a controlled environment. Early indication points to a kernel path that becomes expensive for the new attention pattern in v4beta when qprofile-0.9 is applied.

Action items we are executing now:
- Initiating a safe rollback to v3.2/qprofile-0.7 for the BlueForge production pool (low-risk routemod),
- Holding v4beta/0.9 in canary on a throttled lane,
- We will run a comparative benchmark and post the artifacts to the incident runbook.

We’ll be on the 17:30 ET bridge (invite to follow). Appreciate the sample request IDs and the trimmed logs — keep them coming.

—Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Engineering — Redwood Inference

On Fri, 17 May 2028 at 15:23 Sam Wells <sam.wells@blueforge.com> wrote:
> Marissa,
>
> We pushed the Redwood-provided model upgrade (v3.2 -> v4beta) with the recommended quant profile earlier this morning....
summary: BlueForge reported a sharp P99 latency increase, throughput drop, and elevated 5xx errors shortly after Redwood-delivered model/quant upgrade. Redwood CS and execs authorized an immediate rollback plan, opened incident INC-20280517-BF, and scheduled an executive triage call. Action items include rollback to v3.2/qprofile-0.7, canarying v4beta, and preparing a potential SLA credit for impacted windows.
